content: Desonide is a topical medication prescribed to alleviate redness, swelling, itching, and discomfort associated with various skin conditions. It belongs to a class of drugs known as topical corticosteroids and works by activating natural substances in the skin to reduce inflammation and irritation. Desonide is available in cream, ointment, and lotion forms, and it is typically applied to the skin two or three times daily. It is important to apply the medication at the same times each day and to follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Use desonide exactly as directed; do not apply more or less than prescribed, and do not use it on other areas of your body or for other skin conditions unless instructed by your doctor. Improvement in your skin condition should occur within the first two weeks of treatment. If your symptoms do not improve during this time, contact your doctor. Desonide is intended for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not ingest the medication. To apply, use a small amount of the cream, ointment, or lotion to cover the affected area with a thin, even layer, and gently rub it into the skin. If applying desonide to a child’s diaper area, avoid using tight-fitting diapers or plastic pants. Do not wrap or bandage the treated area unless specifically instructed by your doctor. If your doctor advises you to use a wrap or bandage, follow these steps: 1. Wash or soak the affected area thoroughly. 2. While the skin is still moist, gently rub the medication into the affected area. 3. Cover the area with plastic wrap (e.g., Saran Wrap® or Handi-Wrap®). For hands, feet, or the scalp, you may use plastic gloves, plastic bags, or a shower cap, respectively. 4. If the area is moist, leave the edges partially unsealed or puncture the wrap to allow excess moisture to escape. 5. Leave the plastic wrap in place for the duration specified by your doctor, typically no more than 12 hours per day. 6. Cleanse the skin and reapply the medication each time you use a new plastic wrap. Do not stop using desonide abruptly without consulting your doctor. Desonide may also be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its use for other conditions, ask your doctor or pharmacist. Before using desonide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to desonide or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking, especially medications that suppress the immune system (e.g., azathioprine, cyclosporine, methotrexate, sirolimus, tacrolimus). Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for side effects. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have a history of diabetes, Cushing’s syndrome, circulation problems, or immune system disorders such as AIDS or SCID. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while using desonide, contact your doctor immediately. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while using desonide. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed application. Desonide may cause side effects. Minor side effects include stinging, burning, irritation, peeling, dryness, redness, or itching of the skin. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, though uncommon, include redness, swelling, oozing pus, or other signs of infection at the application site, as well as severe rashes. Children using desonide may experience slowed growth or delayed weight gain. Discuss the risks of using this medication on your child’s skin with their doctor. If you experience serious side effects, you or your doctor may report them to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store desonide in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. If you apply more desonide than prescribed or use it for longer than directed, you may experience an overdose, which can have systemic effects. Contact your doctor immediately if you suspect an overdose or experience unusual symptoms. Keep all appointments with your doctor and any recommended laboratory tests to monitor your response to desonide. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Desonide is sold under brand names such as Tridesilon® and DesOwen®.
